title: Multinomial PMF and MGF Formalization
description: Explores integrating the multinomial distribution into Mathlib's PMF framework. Proves marginal distributions are binomial, states the covariance structure Cov(Xi,Xj) = -n·pi·pj, and documents the ENNReal conversion roadmap for full PMF integration.

overview.historicalContext: The multinomial distribution generalizes the binomial to multiple outcomes. Its properties (marginal distributions, covariance structure) are well-known in probability theory. Integration with Mathlib's formal PMF framework requires converting between real-valued and ENNReal-valued formulations.
overview.problemStatement:
**Question**: Can the multinomial PMF be integrated into Mathlib's PMF framework?

**Answer**: The mathematical content (normalization) is proved. The remaining work is ENNReal type conversion — bookkeeping rather than mathematics. Marginal distributions and covariance structure are formalized.
overview.text: Partial integration of the multinomial distribution into Mathlib's PMF framework, with marginal distribution results and covariance structure.
overview.proofStrategy:
1. Restate multinomial probability from parent
2. Show 2-outcome marginal equals binomial PMF
3. State covariance Cov(Xi,Xj) = -n·pi·pj
4. Document ENNReal conversion roadmap
keyInsights: **Marginals are binomial**: Summing over all other components yields Binomial(n, pi) for each Xi.
**Negative covariance**: Cov(Xi,Xj) = -n·pi·pj is always ≤ 0, reflecting the constraint Σ Xi = n.
**PMF integration is bookkeeping**: The math (normalization) is done; the remaining work is ℝ → ℝ≥0∞ type conversion.

sections.title: Multinomial Probability
sections.summary: Restates the multinomial probability function and normalization from the parent file.

sections.title: Marginal Distributions Are Binomial
sections.summary: Shows the 2-outcome marginal of the multinomial equals the binomial PMF.

sections.title: Covariance Structure
sections.summary: States the covariance formula $\text{Cov}(X_i, X_j) = -np_ip_j$ and the uniform correlation $\rho = -1/(m-1)$.
sections.mathContext: The negative covariance reflects the constraint $\sum X_i = n$: more of one outcome means less of another.

crossReferences.description: Extends the multinomial distribution formalization with marginal results and PMF integration analysis.

conclusion.summary: The multinomial distribution's marginal distributions are binomial, its covariance structure is Cov(Xi,Xj) = -n·pi·pj, and full PMF integration requires ENNReal type conversion (bookkeeping, not mathematics).
conclusion.implications: The mathematical content for PMF integration is complete. A follow-up should perform the ENNReal conversion using ENNReal.ofReal and the existing normalization proof.
